description: franklin_sol_base_refill.py is now 1006 lines (builder-flagged, >800-line guideline in .claude/rules/coding-style.md). This review's own concrete instance of what that growth cost: a fail-closed ledger-append helper now exists in TWO separate implementations in the same file with genuinely identical logic (catch any exception from deps['append_ledger'], print a FATAL line to stderr naming the row's step/status and the exception's class name, sys.exit(1)) -- run_refill's own inline `safe_append_ledger` closure (lines 229-247, pre-existing, untouched per the docstring's stated reason: 'without touching that already-adversary-reviewed function's body') and the NEW module-level `_safe_append_ledger_factory` (lines 193-211) built specifically so run_gas_refill could get 'the identical guarantee run_refill's own inline copy already has'. The stated reason for not sharing (avoid re-touching already-reviewed code) is defensible in isolation, but it leaves two copies of money-safety-critical fail-closed logic that must now be kept in sync by hand -- if the FATAL message format, the exit code, or the exception-handling scope of one copy is ever changed during a future fix, the other copy will silently drift unless a reviewer notices both exist. This is a direct, traceable structural cost of the file's size/scope growth, not merely an abstract line-count concern.
remediation: Extract a single module-level `_safe_append_ledger_factory` (already written) and have run_refill call it too instead of keeping its own inline copy -- this is a mechanical, behavior-preserving refactor (the two implementations are already byte-for-byte equivalent in observable behavior) that removes the drift risk without re-litigating run_refill's already-reviewed logic. Consider this alongside a broader split of franklin_sol_base_refill.py (e.g. extracting run_refill/run_gas_refill's shared production-wiring helpers into their own module) if a future pass adds a third mode.
